Environmental Conditions And Procedures
1. Environment - The Policy
The Company will comply with the environmental policy statement.
2. Materials

Before recommending or using materials within a contract, the Company will liaise closely with the Employer's Designated Representative for procurement, in order to be satisfied that the material satisfies the Employer's criteria for safety, quality, fitness-for-purpose and environmental performance. The Company will make all aware of the environmental factors associated with the proposed material, where possible such as:
a. Emissions and contamination affecting the well being of users during and after use.
b. The extent to which the materials can be recycled, and the recycled content of the materials.
c. Problems arising from disposal after use.
d. The Company will provide a statement of known, adverse, environmental impacts in the production cycles of any materials that the contractor is proposing.
3. Environmental Plan
3.1. Tender Stage

At the tender stage, the Employer will be asked to supply the Company a brief, written description of the Employer's environmental requirements associated with the proposed works. When The Company submits a tender for the proposed works, this will include a environmental plan as part of the health and safety plan, which addresses each of the environmental risks described in, or inferred from the tender documents or site visit.
3.2. Contract Stage

If the Company is successful with the tender and is subsequently awarded the contract then the Company will submit a detailed Environmental Plan not later than four weeks of the date of award of this contract and, in any event, before the start of work on site. This Environmental Plan shall include details of the approach and structure of the necessary environmental management employed in this contract, and in particular, it shall address the following:
a. Environmental Policy Statement.

b. Organisation and arrangements for environmental management. Particular reference shall be made to the site arrangements and procedures for ensuring compliance with environmental legislation, regulations, codes of practice and relevant British Standards and other international standards.

c. Those persons within the organisation who will be responsible for coordinating and monitoring the environmental performance on site and reporting these matters to the Contractor's Board of Directors.
d. Environmental risks assessments for those processes with the greatest environmental risks.
e. The procedures for dealing with hazardous substances and other pollutants.
f. The procedures for reporting and investigating accidents.
g. The procedures for assessing the suitability of subcontractors with respect to environmental issues and how they intend to control their environmental performance.
4. Legal Requirements
1. Compliance with the law.

The Company will carry out the works under the contract in compliance with the requirements of all EC Directives and UK law, and shall pay particular regard to the environmental legislation including any subordinate measures made thereunder, and any changes made to them from time to time.
4.2 Applicable legislation

The Company will consider the environmental legislation be aware of the works processes employed, together with the relevant environmental legislation which applies to each process. The key legislation may include, and is not restricted to, the Acts and Regulations.
4.3 Compliance with Regulations and Codes of Practice

The Company will comply at all times with any other mandatory requirements, local safety and security regulations, including and requirements specified by any regulatory authority, Local Authorities and the requirements set out. The Company will ensure that all operatives are carried out in accordance with the various approved Codes of Practice and Guidance Notes issued by the regulatory authorities, the Department of the Environment, the Department of Transport and applicable local authorities.
4.4 Compliance with the H&S Policy and CDM
The Company will ensure that all operations are conducted in accordance with the latest edition of the Health & Safety Policy.

The Company will ensure that all relevant statutory notices are posted, and the Principal Contractor (CDM) shall specifically display, in a legible condition and in a position where they can be readily seen by any worker on the Project, the particulars of the Project, the Planning Supervisor, the Principal Contractor and other such items as may be required.

The Company/Principal Contractor (CDM) will further ensure that all directly employed staff are made aware of the relevant contents of the Environmental plan, and that employed Subcontractors have suitable arrangements for similarly making their staff aware of the sections of the Environmental Plan applicable to their work.
5. Responsibilities
The Company’s Designated Representative for Environmental Compliance.

The Company will designate one of its employees as the person with responsibility for health, safety and environmental management and compliance of the commissioned works. This person shall have overall responsibility for assessing the environmental risks of the proposed works, developing the Environmental Plan, Method Statements and putting into place a working system which ensures that the correct procedures are followed and ensures compliance with environmental laws, any other regulatory and statutory requirements, and minimises of environmental risks.
The designated person shall be responsible for the following:
a. Liaison with the Employer's Designated Representative, concerning all environmental matters relevant to the works.
b. The auditing of site activities to ensure that the correct environmental management procedures are followed.
c. Keeping controlled records in accordance with the contract/Project Management Procedures.
6. Training

The Company’s Designated Environmental Representative will have the necessary training and credentials to ensure that they understand the technical requirements for compliance with these contract environmental conditions. The scale and extent of the training should be in proportion to the scale and significance of the environmental impacts of the works processes employed.
7. Accidents and Emergencies - Environment
7.1 Contingency Plans

In the event of any possible accident with a serious environmental consequence with a medium to high probability of occurrence, the Company will make contingency plans to minimise the potential environmental risks of an accident. Within the contingency plans, The Company will include procedures to remedy all environmental damage caused by the accident.
7.2 Documentation and Notification of Incidents

Any accident or non-compliance with this contract shall be reported in writing by the Company to the Employer within 24 hours after it occurs. The report shall state the time, date, location and nature of the non-compliance or accident. The report shall explain also how the accident or non-compliance occurred.
7.3 Control Procedures

Before starting work, the Company will develop and document procedures and working practices which specify and instruct all applicable staff and subcontractors in the applicable environmental management procedures to be used on site in order to ensure compliance with the requirements of the contract environmental conditions.
7.4 Records

The Company will maintain for a period of six years, any records of any audits, non-compliance's and accidents; these records shall be available for inspection upon request by the Employer's Designated Representatives, and the Employer's Environmental Auditors. The records of any audits, accidents and non-compliance shall be kept with the Company copy of the environmental plan.
8. Waste Management
8.1 Statutory Duties
The Company will comply with the requirements of the Environmental Protection Act 1990, in respect of waste management duties.
8.2 Duty of Care

The Company will comply with the requirements relating to duty of care in relation to managing controlled and special waste, and shall take steps to ensure that all the appropriate licenses are obtained for the safe management and disposal of waste.

The Company will supply to the Employer copies of site licences before it undertakes waste-management works. The Company will ensure that they store waste correctly. Transfers to licensed tip-sites shall be properly documented, and carried out only by licensed carriers.
8.3 Controlled Waste (other than Special Waste)

Within 4 weeks of the award of the contract, and in any cases before commencement of works, the Company will provide to the Employer details of its practices for the disposal of waste in accordance with the Waste Management Licensing Regulations, 1994, and its Duty of Care under the Environmental Protection Act 1990 (Part 2 Section 34).
8.4 Fly Tipping

The Company will ensure no fly tipping occurs either directly by itself, or its staff or agents, or indirectly through third parties, sub-contracted to dispose of waste. Loads shall only be deposited at licensed tips or other holding current waste management licences.

To ensure the correct management and depositing of controlled waste, The Company will operate a ticket system confirming to the EPA Duty of Care Code of Practice. The ticketing system must be capable of generating reports and provide an audit trail when the Employer requires the tracing of a particular load.
8.5 Hazardous and Special Waste
The Company will provide to the Employer details of its practices for the disposal of Special Wastes. (Special Waste includes, but is not limited to asbestos, PCBs, Halons, CFCs).
8.6 Litter

The Company will ensure that its method of working does not cause litter or rubbish to accumulate, nor encourage others to drop litter, on the premises. The Company will inspect the works site at the end of each working period, and remove and dispose properly of any litter or rubbish.
8.7 Protection of Controlled Waste
Spillages

The Company will report promptly to the Employer all spillage's that occur on the Employer's property. This requirement extends to any spillage's regardless of whether they are discharging directly into a watercourse or not. When making contingency plans. The Company will clearly state the responsibility within the organisation for cleaning up any spillages.
8.8 Discharge Consents
The Company will comply with the Water Resources Act 1991, and the Water Industry Act 1991.
8.9 Control of Spillages

The Company will ensure that all fuel stores, and plant and equipment, which are powered by diesel fuel, have suitable and sufficient bunding underneath them in order to contain the entire contents of any spillage's or leaks. All fuel drums shall be returned to the fuel store after use.
8.10 Disposal of Seepage and Waste Water
The Company will ensure that any seepage and wastewater arising from the works under this contract is collected and discharged via a settlement tank.
9. Nuisances - Noise, Dust, Odours, Vibration, Visibility
And Smoke
9.1 Nuisance

The Company will ensure by use of best practicable means, that the method of working minimises any nuisances derived from noise, smells, fumes, dust, smoke vibration or air pollution associated with the works under this contract.
9.2 Burning of Rubbish
The Company will not burn rubbish or undertaken any other activity likely to give rise to dark smoke on or from the premises.
Where work is within (or near to) an area providing a habitat for a protected species, appropriate measures shall be taken by the Contractor to protect these habitats from the effects of these works.
10. Preservation Of Archaeology

During the works, if the Company discovers archaeological remains, then the Company will proceed with all due care ensuring that the project works do not interfere with the archaeological remains and shall notify the Employers as soon as practical of its discovery.
11. Contaminated Land
11.1 Prevention of Contaminated Land

The Company will ensure that the contamination of land is prevented. In the event that the activities of The Company cause spillage's, leaks, seepage's or deposits of substances which lead to (or in the reasonable opinion of the Employer, could lead to) the contamination of land, then the Company will inform the employer of the problems.
12. Planning Sites With Consideration To Members Of The Public

It is a sound policy to ensure that good relationships are maintained with prospective purchasers and near neighbours. To this end, the following matters will be taken into account when commencing and planning work on site.

Check that site boundaries are clearly identified to avoid disputes with adjoining sites or property: Make contact with persons in the vicinity of who are likely to be affected by building operations.
Make early contact with local authority representatives or other parties to agree means of protection over or against public roads, footpaths or right of way.
Ensure that adequate lighting, adequate protection; warning signs and lighting are available at all times.
Erect all warning signs in agreed positions and in accordance with company policy.
Make arrangements to reduce noise and smoke pollution on site to the minimum possible. Ensure that all plant and equipment is safe at the end of each working day.
Regularly check procedures for preventing pollution by chemicals and fumes.
Ensure that emergency notices are displayed in the site compound is that they are readily visible to all whom may require them.
Ensure that appropriate fire fighting equipment is supplied.
Ensure that all materials are stacked in safe and secure positions and do not present a hazard to children, visitors and occupiers on the site.
Provide special support racks for roof trusses and ensure that lockable dry storage is available for hazardous materials and these are removed from the working area at the end of each day.

If The Company discovers that land on which it is working has been contaminated, or The Company suspects that land on which it has been working is contaminated by some other party, then The Company will notify the Employer immediately in writing.
13. Site Management And Housekeeping
13.1 General Conditions

The Company will keep the site clean, tidy and in a sanitary condition and where applicable comply with the requirements if the Environmental Protection Act with respect to litter and refuse. Rubbish shall not be allowed to accumulate.
Any temporary works, construction plant, or material which for the time being are not required for use on the works shall be stored on site in an orderly manner.
The Company will follow a good housekeeping policy and as a minimum shall comply with the following:
a. Prohibit open fires
b. Remove rubbish at frequent intervals, at least daily
c. Inspect regularly and if necessary repaint and/or repair site fencing and gates. as a minimum, site fencing shall be repainted annually
d. Remove waste food
e. Keep toilet facilities clean
f. Maintain wheel washing facilities and brush clean frequently
g. Carry out an inspection of the site with LUL's representatives at agreed interval and within 3 days, make good all matters identified as requiring rectification
13.2 Site Hazards

The Company will ensure that flammable materials such as paper, cardboard, oily rags do not accumulate. Spillage of hazardous liquids shall be mopped up immediately or absorbed in sand or other suitable material, which shall be disposed of by the Contractor in a manner appropriate to the spillage.
14.0 Complaints
The company will follow the below procedure to deal with environmental complaints:
Complaint Registration and Documentation:
Designate a central point of contact to receive and manage environmental complaints.
Ensure complaints are documented systematically, including details such as complainant information, complaint description, date, and any supporting evidence provided.
Initial Assessment:
Review the complaint to determine its validity and relevance to the company's environmental impact.
If the complaint is outside the company's scope or jurisdiction, provide the complainant with appropriate guidance or refer them to the relevant authority.
Investigation and Gathering of Information:
Assign responsible personnel to conduct a thorough investigation into the complaint.
Gather all relevant information, including any supporting documents or evidence related to the complaint.
Consult relevant internal departments or external experts if necessary to assess the validity of the complaint.
Evaluation and Analysis:
Evaluate the complaint and associated evidence against applicable environmental regulations, company policies, and industry standards.
Analyze the potential environmental impact and severity of the issue raised in the complaint.
Determine if the complaint indicates a systematic problem that requires broader corrective actions.
Communication with Complainant:
Acknowledge receipt of the complaint promptly, expressing appreciation for bringing the matter to our attention.
Provide a designated point of contact to address any concerns or questions the complainant may have during the process.
Keep the complainant informed of the investigation progress and estimated timeline for resolution.
Corrective Actions and Resolution:
If the complaint is valid and actionable, develop and implement appropriate corrective actions to address the environmental issue.
Set realistic timelines for resolving the problem and communicate these to the complainant.
Monitor the implementation of corrective actions to ensure their effectiveness and document the steps taken.
Follow-up and Closure:
Notify the complainant of the actions taken to address the complaint and the resolution achieved.
Seek feedback from the complainant to assess their satisfaction with the response and resolution.
Close the complaint file and maintain records of the complaint, investigation, actions taken, and closure details.
Continuous Improvement:
Conduct periodic reviews of environmental complaints and their resolutions to identify patterns, trends, or recurring issues.
Use the information obtained to enhance environmental management systems, policies, and practices.
Communicate lessons learned to relevant stakeholders and incorporate feedback into future complaint handling procedures.
15.0 Discharging legal responsibilities
The company will follow the below procedure to ensure that it’s legal responsibilities are discharged:
Regulatory Framework Awareness:
Establish a process to stay informed about relevant environmental laws, regulations, and permits applicable in the UK.
Designate responsible personnel or a team to monitor updates and changes in environmental legislation.
Regularly review and update the company's knowledge base on the legal requirements to ensure accurate and up-to-date information.
Legal Requirements Assessment:
Identify the specific environmental legal obligations that apply to the company's operations, activities, and industry sector.
Evaluate the legal requirements based on the nature, scale, and potential environmental impact of the company's activities.
Seek legal counsel or engage environmental experts if necessary to interpret complex regulations or obligations.
Compliance Action Plan:
Develop a comprehensive action plan to address and fulfill the identified legal requirements.
Clearly define responsibilities, timelines, and resources required for compliance.
Allocate necessary budget and resources to implement the compliance action plan effectively.
Implementation of Compliance Measures:
Execute the action plan by implementing specific measures to ensure compliance with environmental laws and regulations. Examples of compliance measures may include:
Establishing procedures to prevent pollution and monitor environmental performance.
Conducting regular environmental audits or assessments.
Developing and implementing appropriate waste management and recycling practices.
Ensuring proper handling, storage, and disposal of hazardous substances.
Obtaining required environmental permits or licenses.
Monitoring and reporting environmental data as required by law.
Documentation and Record Keeping:
Maintain accurate and organized records to demonstrate compliance with environmental legal responsibilities.
Document relevant permits, licenses, assessments, audits, and reports as evidence of compliance.
Establish a centralized system or database to store and manage environmental compliance records for easy access and retrieval.
Training and Awareness:
Provide regular training and awareness programs for employees on their environmental responsibilities and the relevant legal requirements.
Ensure employees understand their roles in meeting environmental legal obligations and the potential consequences of non-compliance.
Foster a culture of environmental compliance and encourage employees to report any potential breaches or concerns.
Monitoring and Auditing:
Establish a monitoring and auditing system to assess ongoing compliance with environmental laws and regulations.
Conduct regular internal audits to evaluate the effectiveness of compliance measures and identify areas for improvement.
Engage external auditors or consultants periodically to conduct independent environmental audits, if necessary.
Non-Compliance Response and Corrective Actions:
Promptly address any identified non-compliance with environmental legal requirements.
Investigate the causes of non-compliance and take immediate corrective actions to rectify the situation.
Implement measures to prevent reoccurrence of non-compliance and improve environmental management systems.
Regulatory Reporting and Communication:
Establish a process for reporting required environmental data and information to regulatory authorities as per legal obligations.
Ensure accurate and timely submission of reports, notifications, or other required documentation.
Maintain open lines of communication with relevant regulatory authorities, promptly addressing any inquiries or requests for information.
Continuous Improvement:
Periodically review and update the company's environmental legal obligations and compliance measures to reflect changes in legislation or industry standards.
Learn from past non-compliance incidents or audits to continuously improve environmental management practices and prevent future breaches
16.0 Supplier evaluation:

Objective: The objective of this procedure is to check if suppliers have environmental procedures in place and comply with environmental standards. By evaluating our suppliers, we can assess their environmental performance and promote sustainability in our supply chain.
Procedure Steps:
Identify Critical Suppliers:
Identify suppliers whose products or services have a significant environmental impact or are related to our environmental objectives.
Set Evaluation Criteria:
Define criteria based on environmental regulations, industry standards, and our environmental policy.
Examples include waste management, energy and water usage, emissions control, recycling efforts, and compliance with environmental laws.
Review Documentation:
Request suppliers to provide relevant documentation, such as environmental policies, permits, certifications, and reports.
Assess the provided documentation to ensure it aligns with our evaluation criteria.
Evaluate the effectiveness and adequacy of their environmental procedures based on the documents.
Prepare Evaluation Report:
Create a report for each supplier, summarizing findings from the documentation review and, if applicable, the on-site audit.
Highlight non-compliance and areas for improvement.
Rate the supplier's environmental performance based on the evaluation criteria.
Share the report with the supplier, clearly communicating non-compliance and improvement expectations.
Corrective Actions and Follow-up:
Request suppliers to develop and implement corrective actions within a specified timeframe if non-compliances are identified.
Provide guidance and support to suppliers in making necessary improvements.
Follow up with suppliers to verify effective implementation of corrective actions.
Maintain Records:
Keep records of supplier evaluations, including documentation reviews, audit reports, evaluation reports, and follow-up actions.
Store the records in a centralized system for easy access.
Continuous Improvement:
Regularly review and update the evaluation criteria to reflect changes in environmental regulations, industry standards, and organizational objectives.
Improve the supplier evaluation process based on feedback and lessons learned.
